props.title: How a transformer attention layer works
props.description: Queries, keys and values, with the maths and a worked example

props.content:
**Attention lets every word look at every other word and decide which ones matter for it.** In "the cat sat on the mat", the word *sat* needs to know **who** sat, so it should pay most attention to *cat*. Each word starts as a vector $x_i$ (its embedding). The layer turns it into three new vectors with three learned matrices: - a **query** $q_i = x_i W_Q$: what this word is looking for - a **key** $k_j = x_j W_K$: what each word offers - a **value** $v_j = x_j W_V$: the information each word passes on ```mermaid flowchart LR X["Input words
(embeddings X)"] --> WQ["× W_Q"] --> Q["Queries Q"] X --> WK["× W_K"] --> K["Keys K"] X --> WV["× W_V"] --> V["Values V"] Q --> S["Scores
Q · Kᵀ / √d_k"] K --> S S --> SM["softmax
(each row sums to 1)"] SM --> M["× V
weighted mix"] V --> M M --> O["Output:
each word, now with context"] ``` The whole layer is one formula: $$ \mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{Q K^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V $$ 1. **Score.** $q_i \cdot k_j$ measures how well word $j$ answers word $i$'s question. A big dot product means "relevant". 2. **Scale.** Divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$ (the key size, e.g. $\sqrt{64} = 8$) so the scores do not grow with the vector size and push softmax into near 0 or 1 values. 3. **Normalise.** Softmax turns each row of scores into weights that add up to 1: $\alpha_{ij} = \frac{e^{s_{ij}}}{\sum_{k} e^{s_{ik}}}$. 4. **Mix.** Each output is the weighted average of the values: $z_i = \sum_{j} \alpha_{ij} \, v_j$.

**What the weights look like.** Each row is one word asking; each column is a word being looked at. The numbers below are made up to show the pattern a trained layer tends to learn: *sat* puts 45% of its attention on *cat* (its subject), and *on* looks most at *sat* and *mat*.

**Multi-head attention** runs this several times in parallel with different $W_Q, W_K, W_V$, so one head can track grammar (who did what) while another tracks position or meaning. The heads' outputs are joined and mixed by one more matrix $W_O$:

$$
\mathrm{MultiHead}(X) = \mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1, \dots, \mathrm{head}_h)\, W_O
$$

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  X["X"] --> H1["Head 1"]
  X --> H2["Head 2"]
  X --> H3["…"]
  X --> H8["Head h"]
  H1 --> C["Concat"]
  H2 --> C
  H3 --> C
  H8 --> C
  C --> WO["× W_O"] --> Y["Output"]
```

| Piece | Shape (n words, model size d, h heads) |
| --- | --- |
| Input $X$ | $n \times d$ |
| $Q, K, V$ per head | $n \times d_k$, with $d_k = d / h$ |
| Weights $\mathrm{softmax}(QK^{\top}/\sqrt{d_k})$ | $n \times n$ |
| Output | $n \times d$ (same as the input, so layers stack) |

In a decoder like GPT, a **mask** sets the scores for future words to $-\infty$ before softmax, so each word can only attend to words before it.
